$description: Tokens the system needs that Figma has no place to hold. Authored here so that a design value still lives in exactly one place. The normalization of a Figma export never touches this file.

layer.$description: Stacking order: the named layer a component occupies when things overlap. Each layer is named for what it holds.

width.$description: Width of the expanded sidebar. Not a step on any primitive scale.

modal.$description: The greatest width of a modal at each size. Fixed frame widths in Figma with no variable behind them; they should become variables.

width.$description: Width of a drawer from the left or right edge. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Least width of the dropdown menu panel, which grows from it to fit its longest item on one line. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

max-width.$description: Greatest width of the dropdown menu panel: past it a long item's words wrap inside the panel. Not in Figma, which draws the panel at one width.

width.$description: Width of the command palette. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Width of the search field in the wide app bar. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

narrow.$description: Width of Figma's phone frames, used for the narrow previews of components that reflow. Not a viewport step; the steps in the size foundation are the layout breakpoints.

width.$description: Width of the table of contents card. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it.
Width of the popover panel. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Width of the control in a side-by-side field, the label taking the rest of the row. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

Width of the note beside, under or at the end of a button: beside it, the note stays there while this much room is left after the button and moves under it otherwise. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

date-min-width.$description: Least width of the date field beside the time field in a date and time picker; with less room the time field moves under it. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

time-width.$description: Width of the time field beside the date field in a date and time picker. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

sort-width.$description: Width of the sort list in a wide filter bar, beside the search field and the filters button. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

field-width.$description: Width of a field in a toolbar: the list that picks what the bar acts on, a search field, a time range. A fixed frame width in Figma (the Picker, the Filter tools' search) with no variable behind it; it should become one.

plot-height.$description: Height of a line or bar chart's plot, the grid lines and the marks between its value labels. A fixed frame height in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

donut.$description: Width and height of a donut chart's ring. A fixed frame size in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

progress-ring.$description: Width and height of a progress ring at each size. Fixed frame sizes in Figma with no variable behind them; they should become variables.

width.$description: Greatest width of the color area, which is square and fills the width it is given up to this. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Width of the color picker panel. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

text-size.$description: The viewport width at and above which the text size context switches from min to max. Aliases an existing viewport step rather than introducing a new measurement.

layout.$description: The viewport width at and above which the page counts as wide for layout. Below it, components that reflow for narrow spaces take their narrow form. Aliases the same viewport step as the text-size switch, so the two change together.

side-columns.$description: The viewport width at and above which a documentation page has room for a column on each side of its content: the sidebar on one side, the table of contents on the other. Between the layout switch and this width the page keeps one side column: the table of contents moves into the page and the sidebar starts as its column of icons. Aliases an existing viewport step rather than introducing a new measurement.

bold.$description: Figma's primitives stop at semibold, but its components set titles and button labels in Geist Bold. It lives here rather than in Figma.

fallback.$description: What a browser draws each family in until its web font has arrived, or if it never does, so the page draws in a sans close to the real one and barely moves when the real one arrives. The token build writes each family's stack after it in every text style that names it; the bundle writes each stand-in face, a font already on the reader's device scaled and spaced to match, into the font style sheets. The measures are each font's own (Capsize's metrics, as Next.js uses them), against Arial, and Geist Mono's against Courier New. Figma has no place for any of it.

stack.$description: What follows Geist in every text style that names it: its stand-in face, then the system's own.

local.$description: The fonts already on the reader's device that the stand-in face draws with: Arial, or Helvetica where Arial is missing.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Arial so its average letter is as wide as Geist's.

ascent.$description: Geist's height above the baseline, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

descent.$description: Geist's depth below the baseline, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

line-gap.$description: Geist's extra room between lines, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

stack.$description: What follows Funnel Display in every text style that names it: its stand-in face, then the system's own.

local.$description: The fonts already on the reader's device that the stand-in face draws with: Arial, or Helvetica where Arial is missing.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Arial so its average letter is as wide as Funnel Display's.

ascent.$description: Funnel Display's height above the baseline, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

descent.$description: Funnel Display's depth below the baseline, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

line-gap.$description: Funnel Display's extra room between lines, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

stack.$description: What follows Geist Mono in every text style that names it: its stand-in face, then the system's own.

local.$description: The fonts already on the reader's device that the stand-in face draws with: Courier New, or Courier where it is missing.

size-adjust.$description: How much the stand-in face scales Courier New so its average letter is as wide as Geist Mono's.

ascent.$description: Geist Mono's height above the baseline, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

descent.$description: Geist Mono's depth below the baseline, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

line-gap.$description: Geist Mono's extra room between lines, as a share of the stand-in face's scaled size.

typography.$description: Weight variants of the Figma text styles that Figma has no text style for; its components apply the weight as an override on top of the regular style. They live here, not in Figma.

body-lg-bold.$description: Body LG in bold: a title over body text.

heading-2xs-bold.$description: Heading 2XS in bold: drawer and modal titles.

body-md-bold.$description: Body MD in bold. Kept for the sites built on the system; the system's own components use semibold for button labels.

body-sm-bold.$description: Body SM in bold. Kept for the sites built on the system; the system's own components use semibold for small button labels.

body-md-semibold.$description: Body MD in semibold: button labels.

body-sm-semibold.$description: Body SM in semibold: small button labels.

body-lg-light.$description: Body LG in light: a section's or an opener's lede, where Figma sets Geist Light.

duration.$description: Raw durations, named by their length in milliseconds. Figma has no motion design, so they are authored here. Components never read these; they read a motion purpose.

easing.$description: Raw easing curves, named by the curve they are: deceleration and acceleration only, no bounce and no overshoot. Components never read these; they read a motion purpose.

steep-out.$description: Starts at full speed and settles gently over most of its length.

motion.$description: Motion by purpose (motion.{purpose}.{property}): timing is chosen by purpose, not taste. Each purpose pairs a duration with an easing. Under reduced motion every component drops its movement; these values then go unused.

feedback.$description: Confirming a pointer or focus change: a color shift on hover, a tooltip appearing.

state.$description: A control changing state in place and able to change back: a switch thumb sliding, a caret turning, a progress bar growing.

enter.$description: Something arriving or opening: a drawer sliding in, a modal or menu appearing, an accordion opening.

exit.$description: Something leaving or closing. Shorter than entering, and accelerating away, so a dismissal never holds the reader up.

delay.$description: The delay added per item in a sequence. Keep a sequence short enough that the last item starts within half a second.

hover.$description: A panel that opens while a mouse rests on its opener (a site header's menus): how long the pointer must rest before it opens, so a pointer passing over does not open it, and how long it may be gone before it closes, so it can cross from the opener into the panel. Touch and keyboard never wait; they open on a press.

open-delay.$description: From the pointer arriving on the opener to the panel opening.

close-delay.$description: From the pointer leaving the opener and panel to the panel closing; coming back within it keeps the panel open.

marquee.$description: A continuous strip that scrolls on its own. Runs at a constant speed.

spin.$description: A ring that turns while something is worked on, with no known end: one whole turn per duration, at an even speed, again until the work is done. Stopped under reduced motion.

live-pulse.$description: The pulse of something really live, open or running. A state, never decoration.

loading.$description: A placeholder waiting for its content: the skeleton's sweep, from one edge to the other, again until the content arrives. Stopped under reduced motion.

cursor.$description: A blinking text cursor. Blinks in steps, not with a curve.

ambient.$description: Slow background drift the eye should never have to follow.

chart-entrance.$description: A chart drawing itself the first time it comes into view, once: bars grow from the baseline one after another, a line and its area are uncovered from the start of the plot to its end, a ring sweeps round from the top. Changes after that land at once. Stopped under reduced motion, when the chart is simply there.

grow-duration.$description: How long each bar takes to grow to its height.

reveal-duration.$description: How long a line takes to be uncovered across the plot, or a ring to sweep round.

stagger.$description: The wait added for each bar after the first.

stagger-span.$description: The longest the last bar waits: with many bars the wait per bar shrinks, so the last still starts within half a second.
